stories.headline: PSOE corruption crisis deepens as UCO raids Ferraz, Zapatero imputado, David Sánchez goes on trial, and Sánchez vows to govern until 2027
stories.summary: Spain's ruling Socialist Party faced simultaneous judicial blows in the last week of May: the Guardia Civil's UCO unit searched PSOE headquarters in Ferraz under orders from High Court judge Pedraz (the 'caso Leire Díez' / 'cloacas' case); former PM Zapatero was formally implicated in the Plus Ultra airline rescue case; and PM Pedro Sánchez's brother David went on trial in Badajoz for influence-peddling and malfeasance. Sánchez appeared before the Youth Socialists congress to dismiss the crises as the work of a 'treacherous opposition' and vowed to govern 'until 2027 and beyond,' while requesting a parliamentary appearance; partners PNV and Junts publicly demanded early elections; and multiple polls showed PSOE support falling sharply.

stories.headline: Armed Forces Day 2026 in Vigo marked by flag-falling incident and Princess Leonor's institutional debut
stories.summary: Spain's Día de las Fuerzas Armadas (DIFAS 2026) took place on May 29–30 in Vigo, with King Felipe VI presiding over a naval review and the main parade alongside Queen Letizia and Princess Leonor, the latter making her first appearance at the event near the end of her military training. Bad weather cancelled the aerial display, and a technical failure caused the national flag to fall from its mast during the flag-raising ceremony, prompting the King to order a replacement flag — an incident that generated extensive social media commentary and media analysis.

stories.headline: Pope León XIV prepares for historic June visit to Spain, invited by King Felipe VI
stories.summary: Pope León XIV is scheduled to visit Spain from June 6–12 in a state visit formally invited by King Felipe VI, with stops in Madrid, Barcelona, and Gran Canaria. Media coverage this week focused on logistical preparations in Madrid (traffic disruptions, massive expected crowds), the Pope's agenda themes (poverty, immigration, youth), political dimensions (Sánchez's prior meeting with the Pope in the Vatican, Vox's decision to attend all papal events as a reconciliation gesture toward the Church), and Ayuso's audience with the Pope in Rome ahead of his arrival.

stories.summary: Alberto Núñez Feijóo chose a restrained opposition posture this week despite intensifying PSOE judicial troubles, resisting internal party pressure for a no-confidence motion (moción de censura) by noting insufficient support, while simultaneously accelerating a push into Catalonia with his participation in the Cercle d'Economia forum (June 2) and preparations for a PPC congress. Multiple polls showed PP leading in voting intention, and Feijóo made remarks that he would use 'every possible means' to change the government.

stories.headline: US Ambassador warns Spain to be 'very careful' deepening ties with China
stories.summary: US Ambassador to Spain Benjamin Leon publicly warned Madrid on May 27 that it must exercise caution as it deepens its relationship with China, specifically calling out data, defence, and telecommunications sectors where Beijing seeks dominance. The warning came against a backdrop of strained US-Spain relations over Spain's refusal to meet NATO defence spending commitments and earlier Trump suggestions about possible sanctions.

articles.title: US envoy warns Spain to be 'very careful' in deepening ties with China

stories.headline: Vox distances itself from far-right European extremists while seeking Church rapprochement
stories.summary: Vox this week sent a party spokesperson to the Remigration Summit 2026 in Portugal (a gathering of European white-nationalist ultra groups) while simultaneously pursuing a reconciliation with the Spanish Catholic Church ahead of the Pope's visit, with Abascal confirming attendance at all papal events after months of tension over immigration policy with the Bishops' Conference.

stories.headline: Banco de España issues warnings on housing market risk and mortgage delinquency amid IMF pressure
stories.summary: The Banco de España attracted attention this week with multiple financial stability warnings: the institution alerted about potential mortgage delinquency risks (reportedly up to 6% by 2027 for variable-rate mortgages), cautioned that restricting high-risk mortgages could worsen housing access and rental costs, and urged that irregular immigrants be allowed to open bank accounts. Separately, outgoing ECB Vice-President Luis de Guindos said Spain's seat on the ECB Executive Board was 'perfectly justified' and would be recovered in coming quarters.

stories.headline: Spain blocks prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi for operating without gambling licences
stories.summary: Spain's Consumer Rights Ministry temporarily banned prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi from operating in the country, publishing the order in the official state gazette on May 26. Spanish authorities classify prediction markets as a form of gambling when bets are placed on uncertain outcomes, consistent with similar moves by other European jurisdictions.

articles.title: Spain blocks prediction markets Polymarket, Kalshi over lack of gambling licences

stories.headline: Royal House: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia host Monaco royals for 150th anniversary of bilateral relations
stories.summary: King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia were scheduled to receive Prince Albert II of Monaco and Princess Charlène for a two-day official visit commemorating the 150th anniversary of the Monaco embassy in Spain, including a joint visit to an exhibition at the Real Jardín Botánico. Coverage also noted Felipe VI's appearances at the Corrida de la Prensa at Las Ventas and his remarks to Mexican writer Zunzunegui regarding his earlier comments about colonial abuses.

stories.headline: CNI implicated in Plus Ultra case: Zapatero associate's notebook links intelligence agents to Venezuela prisoner releases and Edmundo González repatriation
stories.summary: Documents seized from the home of Julio Martínez (described as a Zapatero associate in the Plus Ultra case) contained handwritten references to CNI agents allegedly involved in negotiations for the release of Venezuelan prisoners and the repatriation of opposition leader Edmundo González. The High Court judge in the Plus Ultra case is investigating whether the Zapatero-linked network used CNI contacts for what could constitute improper interventions in state affairs. Separately, testimony in the 'Operación Kitchen' trial linked Villarejo to the CNI.

stories.headline: Cercle d'Economia Barcelona annual meeting brings together King, Sánchez, Illa, and Feijóo
stories.summary: The 41st Reunió del Cercle d'Economia was scheduled for June 1–3 in Barcelona, an influential annual business forum where King Felipe VI was to preside over an award ceremony, with President Sánchez, Catalan President Salvador Illa, and PP leader Feijóo all attending. The forum's theme was European strategic autonomy. The gathering acquired particular significance given Spain's political crisis and the presence of key figures across the political divide.

stories.headline: Spain's economy stands out in Europe but structural challenges persist, per US financial press
stories.summary: US financial magazine Global Finance published analysis this week highlighting Spain as a standout European economy — citing record 96.8 million tourists in 2025, Banco de España upward GDP revision to 2.3% for 2026, and a strong banking sector — while also flagging structural risks including housing affordability, labour market duality, and youth unemployment.
